notebookCells.text:
# Brands

A notebook, not a dashboard — here to pin that `# drill` fires from a notebook
cell too. Nothing in this file mentions drill: the tags are on
`orders.brand_name` and `orders.region_name`, so any cell that groups by one of
those dimensions is clickable, and clicking one either leaves for a dashboard or
filters this notebook in place.
## Amount by brand
run: orders -> by_brand
## Orders by region
run: orders -> by_region

# Orders since

A notebook whose parameters are the point. `## autorun=false` asks for an Apply
button, which matters more here than on a dashboard: one parameter change
re-runs every cell in the document.
## Orders in the window
run: orders -> since_totals

# Orders from a start

Where a notebook's controls begin. `## givens { … }` is the notebook spelling of
a dashboard's `# artifact { givens { … } }`: a value the reader arrives at,
rather than the declaration's default. A URL parameter beats it, so a link still
shows what the sender was looking at.
## Orders in the window
run: orders -> since_totals

warnings.subject: artifact_unparsed
warnings.message: Tag does not parse (Expected '{', found '['), so the whole tag is discarded and this file is treated as a shared include rather than a dashboard.
Line 1: `dashboard_columns=8` is a deprecated spelling of the grid width. Fix: write `dashboard { columns=8 }` instead.
Line 1: `dashboard_columns=8` in the artifact tag and `dashboard { columns=12 }` disagree about the grid width. Fix: keep `dashboard { columns=… }` and remove `dashboard_columns`.
Line 2: this `"` note below `## artifact` is the dashboard's description only because nothing sits above the tag. Fix: move it above `## artifact`.
Line 4: the `(markdown)` block `unused` is not named by any entry in `tiles=[…]`, so it is not shown on the dashboard. Fix: delete the block, or list `unused { kind=text }` in `tiles`.
Line 1: this notebook is served from dashboards/, where the other kind is created. It works either way. Fix: move it to notebooks/ if you want folders to match kinds.
Line 1: `source: a is duckdb.sql("select 1 as x")` sits above the `## artifact` tag, and only `##!` flags, `//` comments and `"` notes may. Fix: move it below the artifact tag.
Line 1: this notebook's artifact tag has no `kind`. Fix: write `## artifact { kind=notebook }`.
Line 4: `##| markdown` opens a block that is not on the `(markdown)` route, so its body is not a markdown cell. Did you mean `##|(markdown)`?
Line 8: this comment sits directly above a cell but is not part of it, so the notebook does not show it. Fix: write it as a `##(markdown)` prose note, or move it inside the statement it describes.

list in it.

notebooks.title: Storefront overview
notebooks.description: Revenue, margin and volume for the order lines the controls select, as a story: the summary first, then which way it is moving and where it came from.

notebookCells.text: import { order_items, products } from "storefront.malloy"

Pick a **Category** in the controls above and every chart below re-runs for it.
Leave the control empty to read the whole catalog.
The monthly trend says which way revenue is moving.

#" Revenue by month for the selected category
# line_chart
# label="Revenue by month"
run: order_items -> sales_by_month + { where: category ~ $CATEGORY }
notebookCells.caption: Revenue by month for the selected category

notebookCells.text: The brand ranking says who is behind those numbers.

#" The eight brands with the most revenue in the selected category
# bar_chart
# label="Top brands"
run: order_items -> top_brands + { where: category ~ $CATEGORY }
notebookCells.caption: The eight brands with the most revenue in the selected category

notebookCells.text: Last, the best-selling products, defined once as a named query and then run.
query: top_products_in_category is order_items -> top_products + { where: category ~ $CATEGORY }

#" The ten best-selling products in the selected category
run: top_products_in_category
notebookCells.caption: The ten best-selling products in the selected category
